title: Apleno sequence file (.pseq)
description: A sequence is the flowchart of an Apleno app: a graph of steps executed one after another, starting from the single 'start' step and following each step's 'target'. The file is JSON, edited visually by the Apleno Sequence Editor.

_version.description: Format version. The current version is 4.

cameraX.description: Editor view position (horizontal). Only used by the visual editor.

cameraY.description: Editor view position (vertical). Only used by the visual editor.

cameraZoom.description: Editor zoom level. Only used by the visual editor.

steps.description: All steps of the sequence. Exactly one step must have type 'start'. Step ids must be unique.

id.description: Numeric identifier of the step, unique in the file. Other steps point to this step with 'parameters.target' / 'parameters.targetOnFalse'.

type.description: 'start': entry point of the sequence (exactly one). 'script': runs an R (.R) or Python (.py) script file. 'gui': displays an interface (.pgui file) and waits for the user to submit it. 'condition': evaluates an R/Python expression and goes to 'target' if true, 'targetOnFalse' if false. 'sequence': runs another sequence (.pseq file). 'end': ends the sequence.

x.description: Horizontal position of the step center in the visual editor. Steps are 200x50 and snap to a 50-unit grid; lay them out top to bottom about 150 units apart, with condition branches offset horizontally (e.g. 300 units).

y.description: Vertical position of the step center in the visual editor (y grows downward).

customId.description: Identifier usable from R/Python code to refer to this step (not used for start/end). Must be unique in the sequence when not empty.

customName.description: Name of the step displayed to the end user in the steps list (not used for start/end).

file.description: For 'script', 'gui' and 'sequence' steps: path of the file to run/display, relative to the project root folder (e.g. 'scripts/load.R', 'interfaces/form.pgui', 'sub.pseq').

code.description: For 'condition' steps: R/Python expression returning TRUE/True or FALSE/False.

target.description: Id of the next step (for a condition: the step to go to when the expression is true). Required for every step type except 'end'.

targetOnFalse.description: For 'condition' steps: id of the step to go to when the expression is false.
